speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient with a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics. Can you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were prescribed and for how long?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Induced Morbilliform Drug Eruption.

Based on the history of starting amoxicillin for sinusitis one week ago, followed by the onset of a generalized itchy rash and fever, this is a classic presentation of a delayed-type drug hypersensitivity reaction. The timing (7-10 days post-exposure) and the morphology (starting in flexural areas like antecubital/popliteal fossae) are highly characteristic. Do you have any photos of the rash, and are there any other symptoms like facial swelling or difficulty breathing?
